_about: List rates the batch runners estimate with BEFORE a call is made (data, not code). USD per output second unless stated. Read by scripts/broll/run_world_batch.py and mirrored in src/lib/worldBatch/rates.ts (a test holds the two together). seedance_usd_per_s is the provider's per-second figure for a job WITHOUT a video input, at all three sizes (480p was 0.2468 until 4 October — a different kind of figure, see _seedance_tokens); a job with one (every restage) is priced by seedance_tokens — see _seedance_tokens.
_seedance_tokens: Higgsfield's published rule for Seedance 2.5 (open.higgsfield.ai, model page, 'Price', read 4 October 2026): billable video tokens = ceil(output height x output width x (input video seconds + generated video seconds) x 24 / 1024); 1,000 tokens cost usd_per_1000_tokens for the resolution; when a video input is provided the token rate is multiplied by video_input_factor; both input and generated durations are billable; image and audio references do not count as video input; rates are before any customer discount. SCOPE OF WHAT HAS BEEN CHARGED: five jobs on 3-4 October 2026, all model seedance-2.5-reference, mode reference_to_video, 720p at 9:16 (720 x 1280), one video reference as long as the output (4.004 s for 4 s, 6.006 s for 6 s), one image reference, generate_audio false, no discount applied (the account's discount line read $0.00): the rule gives $2.22 and $3.33 and those are the amounts charged. 480p, 1080p, a source longer or shorter than the output, more than one video reference and audio on have NOT been charged yet: for those the estimate is the published rule, unverified. A discount (the provider offers one against a larger top-up) would lower the charge and is not modelled. THE PROVIDER'S OWN PER-SECOND FIGURES, read from the three model pages on 4 October 2026 (16:9 output): without a video input, per second of generated video — $0.2056 at 480p, $0.4622 at 720p, $1.1372 at 1080p; with a video input, per second of COMBINED input and generated video — $0.1234, $0.2773, $0.6823. The rule reproduces all six from the pixel counts here (854 x 480, 1280 x 720, 1920 x 1080). The $0.2468 that used to stand in seedance_usd_per_s for 480p is neither of those: it is the 'from' headline of the reference-to-video and video-edit pages — two combined seconds (one in, one out) at 480p with a video input, 19,215 tokens x $0.01284, rounded up. It and $0.2056 describe the same model and size under different treatment of the video input and different units of time, and both give the same total for a 4 s restage from a 4 s source: 76,860 tokens = $0.99, or 4 output seconds x $0.2468 = $0.99. CHARGED vs PUBLISHED: seedance_tokens.charged lists the sizes at which a real charge has matched the rule (720p only). 480p and 1080p agree with the provider's published figures and have never been charged: an estimate at those sizes is the published rule, not a verified price.
